chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Three (matters) Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not grant an allowance (rukhsah) for anyone regarding them: paying back the trust to the righteous and the immoral, and fulfilling the covenant with the righteous and the immoral, and being righteous to the parents, whether they were righteous or immoral.

key_terms.أَدَاءُ الْأَمَانَةِ: Paying back or fulfilling the trust
key_terms.رُخْصَة: Allowance or concession in religious obligation

ai.seo_question: What three obligations in Islam must be fulfilled even if the recipient is a sinner?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish that filial piety (Birr al-Walidayn) is an absolute duty, independent of the parents' moral standing, mirroring the unconditional nature of returning trusts and fulfilling covenants. Shia scholars emphasize this to counter the view that one might withhold rights from disobedient parents, highlighting that these three obligations are rooted in divine decree rather than the recipient's merit. This underscores the unique status of parents in Shia jurisprudence, where their rights are upheld even if they are 'fajir' (immoral).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Anbasa Bin Mus’ab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Three (matters), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Give an allowance regarding these – Paying back the entrustment to the righteous and the immoral, and the loyalty with the pact to the righteous and the immoral, and being righteous with the parents, whether they were righteous or immoral’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus’ab from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

‘‘There are three things in which Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has not given any concession: safely returning of the trust to appropriate people, regardless of their being good or evil people, keeping the promise for good or evil people, and being kind to parents whether of good or of evil manners.”
